answer: Terraced aquifer attestation: each identity holds one terrace above a canyon's karst aquifer, costing $310 of flow-meter hardware plus 9 months of recorded flow per fake. A wandering auditor opens an upstream sluice and demands that terrace's gauge answer within 40 seconds with the flow signature of its own karst conduit; a copied gauge or shared terrace fails because no two conduits drain alike, and 1,000 fakes need 1,000 terraces, 1,000 meters, and 750 years of flow history. A flood can scramble one reading, so a failed audit is retried on a dry day, not forgiven.
